title: Larry with an AR-15 aboard a helicopter
description: Larry, wind-tossed and intent, sits inside a helicopter gripping an AR-15 upright beside him — the first time he had ever seen one, he says. The rifle belonged to someone else on the helicopter; he held it and put on an expression for the camera. His assumption is they were heading back to headquarters.
researchNotes: Relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0029-c18035474.json and -c18035478.json). Period detail rings true: in 1964–65 the AR-15 (as it was then called, per Larry) circulated with advisors and special-operations troops before general M16 issue — Larry's own weapon was a Thompson (VN-0013). The serious expression was posed. 'Heading back to headquarters' is Larry's stated assumption, not a memory. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0029-c18416068.json and -c18416092.json): 'Location: Nui Ba Den or Ton Son Nhut' — two candidates, so no place is set — and 'Date: March of 1965 - this is when the new arrivals started showing up with the AR-15. This was the first one I saw.' He dates the frame by the rifle. At VN-0019 he also calls the AR-15 in that picture 'one of the first one's in Vietnam'; which of the two he saw first, if either, is not settled. He adds that 'we had stoners which are the prototype of the AR-15. Just a few special forces camps had them. They didn't have the site or the handle on it but they shot 223.' That is recorded as he said it; for whoever reads it against the history, the Stoner 63 was a separate, later weapon system by the AR-15's designer, also in .223, and the name may have covered more than one early rifle in the talk of the time.
